question: Who led the Chittagong Armoury Raid on 18 April 1930?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Surya Sen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surya Sen**, famously known as **Masterda**, was the chief organizer of the **Chittagong Armoury Raid**, which occurred on **18 April 1930**.
 
• The raid was aimed at overthrowing British colonial rule by capturing arms and disrupting communication lines in **Chittagong**, now in Bangladesh.
 
• Surya Sen was a school teacher and an ardent believer in armed struggle for independence. He was associated with revolutionary groups like **Anushilan Samiti** and **Jugantar**.
 
• The raid involved a group of young revolutionaries, including notable participants such as **Ganesh Ghosh**, **Pritilata Wadedar**, and others who played supporting roles under Surya Sen's leadership.
 
• Following the raid, Surya Sen and his associates faced intense persecution. He was eventually captured by the British and **hanged on 12 January 1934**, but his legacy remains a symbol of courage and sacrifice in India's struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chittagong Armoury Raid:**

 
 
• The raid was planned to seize British arms and ammunition stored at the **Police Armoury** in Chittagong and destroy telegraph and railway lines to disrupt British communication.
 
• The revolutionaries declared the formation of a **Provisional Revolutionary Government** following the raid.
 
• Although the raid was not entirely successful, it inspired subsequent revolutionary activities and highlighted the determination of Indian youth in their fight against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Ghosh:**
 
 
• Ganesh Ghosh was one of the key participants in the raid. He was responsible for leading a group to capture the **Police Armoury** at Chittagong.
 
• After the raid, he continued his involvement in revolutionary activities and later became a member of the **Communist Party of India**.
 
 
 
• **Pritilata Wadedar:**
 
 
• Pritilata Wadedar was a female revolutionary who joined Surya Sen's group and played a significant role in the movement.
 
• She led an attack on the **European Club** in Chittagong in 1932 and sacrificed her life by consuming cyanide to avoid arrest.
 
 
 
• **Anushilan Samiti:**
 
 
• Anushilan Samiti was a revolutionary organization founded in Bengal that played a key role in India's freedom struggle.
 
• It emphasized armed resistance and inspired many young revolutionaries, including Surya Sen, to join the struggle against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Surya Sen:**
 
 
• Surya Sen's leadership in the Chittagong Armoury Raid is remembered as a bold and courageous act of defiance against colonial oppression.
 
• He remains a celebrated figure in Indian history, inspiring generations to fight for justice and independence.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Surya Sen’s philosophy:** He believed in the necessity of armed struggle to achieve independence and inspired many to join the revolutionary movement.
 
• **Impact of the Raid:** While the Chittagong Armoury Raid did not achieve all its objectives, it demonstrated the bravery and commitment of Indian revolutionaries.
 
• **Women’s participation:** The involvement of revolutionaries like Pritilata Wadedar highlighted the role of women in India's independence movement.
 
• **Martyrdom:** Surya Sen’s execution was a great loss, but his sacrifice remains a symbol of resistance and inspiration for future generations.
